hints.content: The *domain* of a function is the set of all inputs for which the function is defined.

According to the graph, $g$ is defined for all inputs between $-6$ and $6$, including both $-6$ and $6$. This means we can write the domain of $g$ as $-6 \leq x \leq 6$.

options.explanation: In most cases outside of this exercise, an image will only show part of the complete graph of a function, so unless we're given further information about the function, we will not be able to tell exactly what the domain of the function is.
options.showPrompt: Can we always tell the domain of a function from its graph?

This point has a line segment that connects to negative four, negative three. A line segment connects negative four, negative three to negative two, six. A line segment connects negative two, six to six, seven. The point six, seven is plotted on the graph. There is a solid horizontal line from negative six, zero to six, zero. Both points are plotted. There is a dotted vertical line from negative six, zero to negative six, three. There is another dotted vertical line from six, zero to six, seven.

hints.content: In conclusion, the domain of the function is $-6 \leq x \leq 6$.
